info.title: Rdio Scanner — System Messages API
info.summary: Post, change and remove the messages listeners see above the scanner display.
info.description:
The System Messages plugin shows notices to everyone listening: system messages ("County Fire is not being received") and maintenance messages ("The server restarts at 22:00"). This API lets another program — a monitoring check, a deploy script, a chat bot — post and manage those messages.

**Keys.** Every request except the one for this document needs an API key, created in the administration page under Plugins → System Messages → API keys. A key is shown once, when it is created. Send it in the `X-API-Key` header, or as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. These keys are separate from the server's upload API keys and from the administrator's login.

**Times.** Times are sent as ISO 8601 date-times with a zone (`2026-03-01T22:00:00Z`) or as a number of milliseconds since the Unix epoch, and are always returned as ISO 8601 in UTC. A message with no `startsAt` shows as soon as it is posted; a message with no `endsAt` shows until it is ended or deleted.

**What listeners see.** A message shows while its state is `active`. Listeners connected at the time are told within a few seconds of any change, without reloading. A listener can close a message; replacing it with `PUT` shows it to them again.

**Limits.** At most 20 messages may be showing or scheduled at once, and at most 500 stored. A request over either limit is refused with 409.

server.description: The address the scanner is served at, without a trailing slash.

get.description: Every stored message, newest first — scheduled, active and ended. With `active=true`, only the messages listeners are being shown right now, in the order they are shown: system messages first, then maintenance, the most recent first within each.

parameters.name: active
parameters.description: Set to `true` to list only what listeners see now.

messages.title: County Fire is not being received
messages.body: The north tower feed dropped at 14:05. We are working on it.

post.description: Stores a message. If it has no `startsAt`, or one that has passed, listeners see it straight away. The `source` of the stored message is the label of the key that posted it.

outage.summary: A system message, showing until it is ended

value.title: County Fire is not being received
value.body: The north tower feed dropped at 14:05. We are working on it.

value.title: Server update tonight
value.body: The scanner will be unavailable for about ten minutes.

put.description: Replaces the whole message: a field left out is cleared, not kept. The `revision` goes up by one, which shows the message again to listeners who had closed it. The `source` is not changed.

value.title: County Fire is partly restored
value.body: The north tower is back. The east tower is still down.

200.description: The message as it now stands.

delete.description: Removes the message altogether. Listeners stop seeing it at once. To take a message down but keep a record of it, end it instead.

post.description: Sets the message's `endsAt` to the present moment, so listeners stop seeing it and it stays in the list as `ended`. Ending a message that has already ended changes nothing and returns it as it is. The request has no body.

get.description: The OpenAPI description of this API, as shipped with the plugin version that is running. No key is needed.

apiKey.name: X-API-Key
apiKey.description: A key created under Plugins → System Messages → API keys.

bearer.description: The same key, for clients that can only send an Authorization header.

MessageId.name: id
MessageId.description: The message's id, as returned when it was posted.

Kind.description: `system` for something wrong or noteworthy with what is being received; `maintenance` for work on the server itself. Listeners see the two under separate headings, system messages first.

SystemColor.description: The colours a `system` message can be shown in, calm to serious: `green` all clear or restored, `teal` information, `purple` a notice, `yellow` degraded, `pink` an outage. The meanings are a convention for whoever posts; the server does not act on them.

MaintenanceColor.description: The colours a `maintenance` message can be shown in: `blue` planned, `amber` starting soon, `orange` running over, `red` under way, `grey` finished or called off. The meanings are a convention for whoever posts; the server does not act on them.

TimeInput.description: A moment in time between the years 2000 and 2100: an ISO 8601 date-time with a zone, or a whole number of milliseconds since the Unix epoch. `null` or left out means none.

color.description: Each kind has its own colours: a `system` message is `green`, `teal`, `purple`, `yellow` or `pink`, and a `maintenance` message is `blue`, `amber`, `orange`, `red` or `grey`. A colour belonging to the other kind is refused with 400. Left out, a system message is `green` and a maintenance message is `blue`.

title.description: The line listeners read first. Plain text; line breaks become spaces.

body.description: More detail, shown under the title. Plain text; line breaks are kept. Markup is shown as written, never interpreted.

linkUrl.description: One link shown with the message. Must begin `http://` or `https://`.

linkLabel.description: The words the link is shown as. Only allowed with `linkUrl`; left out, the link reads "More information".

startsAt.description: When listeners start seeing the message. Left out: as soon as it is posted.

endsAt.description: When listeners stop seeing it; the message is gone at this moment. Must be later than `startsAt`. Left out: it shows until it is ended or deleted.

color.description: One of the kind's colours — see `SystemColor` and `MaintenanceColor`. A message stored by version 1.0 of the plugin keeps the colour it was given, which may be a colour that now belongs to the other kind, until it is replaced. Such a message cannot be sent back unchanged: a replace must give one of the kind's current colours, or leave `color` out to take the default.

startsAt.description: `null` when the message started as soon as it was posted — see `createdAt`.

state.description: `scheduled`: its start is still to come. `active`: listeners are being shown it. `ended`: its end has passed.

revision.description: 1 when posted, one more for each replacement.

source.description: Who posted it: `admin`, or the label of the API key.

error.description: What was wrong, in a sentence.

BadRequest.description: The request was not understood, and nothing was changed.

value.error: linkUrl must be an http:// or https:// address
color for a system message must be one of: green, teal, purple, yellow, pink
id must be a positive whole number

Unauthorized.description: No key was sent, or the key is not one this server knows.

value.error: a valid API key is required, in the X-API-Key header

LimitReached.description: A limit on how many messages may exist was reached, and nothing was changed.

value.error: there are already 20 messages showing or scheduled; end one first

ServerError.description: The server could not complete the request. The server's log says why.

value.error: the server could not complete the request
